newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Firming Australian bonds pause after tender.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Firming Australian bonds pause after tender.

text.p: Australian bonds finished up on the day, but just off their highs, after a solid start to the day saw them rallying ahead of a A$600 million bond tender.
Bonds eased slightly after the tender opened the afternoon trading session but still remained well supported, traders said.

Bonds had ignored a flat to weaker U.S. market to strengthen through the morning. Traders were surprised that not only was the market strengthening ahead of tender, but that the long end had kept pace with the short end.
"Tens were really well bid all morning," one trader said. "Whether somebody lost stock last night, I'm not sure."
In the tender, the A$200 million of April 2000 stock went at a weighted average of 6.579 percent, while the A$400 million of October 2007 stock went a weighted average of 7.583 percent.
Traders said the tender stock was well received by the market, but after rallying into the tender, some softness was was to be expected as the stock was absorbed.
"Given the market had rallied and the U.S. was unchanged to slightly weaker, I think it went pretty well," the trader said.
U.S. CPI and retail sales data for December later today are expected to provide near term direction for the market, ahead of the release of Thursday's employment report for December.

Employment is seen rising only 5,000 in the month, with the unemployment rate rising slightly to 8.6 percent. Traders said such a result, which would be seen as weak, would lift hopes of a first quarter rate cut and be bullish for the short end.

Spreads ended slightly off their early narrowing, but generally outperformed North American debt on the day. NZ bonds were bouyed by a firming market, and contiuing eurokiwi and smaurai issues, ahead of this Friday's CPI data.
